key_insight: A sampled refusal does not establish robustness: substantial probability of harmful continuations can remain hidden beneath a safe response.
engineering_relevance: Measuring harmful reachability alongside attack success rate can distinguish apparently similar models and help prioritize red-team testing.
method: Model autoregressive generation as a stochastic process over token prefixes.
Build a bounded continuation tree and label terminal continuations with a semantic harm evaluator.
Use exact probabilistic model checking to estimate finite-horizon harmful reachability.
evidence_signal: Evaluation across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors reports that bounded continuation analysis reveals hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful red-teaming signal.
watch_item: Results are limited by the continuation bounds and the reliability of the semantic harm evaluator, so they do not establish full-generation safety.
paper_title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
